history.summary: Famous Saraswati temple on the banks of the Godavari at Basara (also spelled Basar), one of the very few temples in India where Saraswati is the presiding deity. Legend: after the Kurukshetra war, Maharishi Vyasa settled in this Dandakaranya spot, made sand murtis of Saraswati, Lakshmi and Kali, and prayed to them; the place was called Vasara and became Basara. The goddess sits holding a veena, bedecked with turmeric. Renowned for the Aksharabhyasam ceremony — formal initiation of children into education — especially on Vasant Panchami and Navratri. Built in South Indian style; one source notes the absence of carvings. CSV town Basara is correct.

name: Sri Gnana Saraswathi Temple (Basara)
town_description: Basara (Basar) is a census town in Nirmal district, Telangana, on the banks of the Godavari river, about 35 km from Nizamabad and 205 km from Hyderabad. It is a major pilgrimage town centred on the Gnana Saraswathi temple, thronged by parents bringing children for Aksharabhyasam.

travel.road: ~34–35 km from Nizamabad, ~70 km from Nirmal, ~205 km from Hyderabad (published distances)
